Session Rates & Options

Clear, predictable options to help you choose what fits your needs. If cost is a barrier, please reach out — I maintain a small sliding scale and limited pro bono slots.

I am out-of-network with most insurers. I provide a superbill you can submit for possible reimbursement. Rates are subject to change; your exact fee will be confirmed when scheduling.
{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}} Ask about sliding scale
Sessions are typically 50 minutes. Some people benefit from extended initial intakes (75–90 minutes) to create a focused plan; that option is available and priced separately.

Common Misunderstandings

Myth

If I book a session, I’m committing to years of therapy.

Reality

Therapy is a collaborative decision. We plan together, and many clients choose brief focused work or intermittent check-ins after an initial block.

Myth

Sliding scale means lower-quality care.

Reality

Sliding scale helps me serve clients with limited means while keeping a balanced caseload. Clinical attention and boundaries are the same.

Myth

If I don’t use insurance, I can’t ever seek reimbursement.

Reality

I provide a superbill that many clients submit to insurers for partial reimbursement. Coverage varies by plan.

Principles That Shape Fees

Transparency

Fees are listed up front. No surprises when you arrive for a session.

Equity

A limited number of reduced-fee slots are reserved to improve access.

Illustrative Client Summaries

Midlife Transition

Client A used a 6-session Brief Focus Package to identify values, experiment with small habit changes, and create a plan for a career pivot. The package structure supported momentum and clear review points.

Managing Burnout

Client B began with weekly sessions and then shifted to biweekly maintenance after 10 sessions. We combined cognitive strategies and behavioral experiments tailored to daily routines.

Relationship Stress

Client C used individual sessions to develop communication skills and boundary-setting before deciding whether to pursue couples work.

Short FAQ about Cost & Logistics

Do you accept insurance?

I am typically out-of-network. I provide superbills to submit to your insurer; reimbursement policies vary.

Is there a sliding scale?

Yes. A very limited number of reduced-fee appointments are available. Please contact me via email to inquire; requests are handled case-by-case.

What forms of payment do you take?

Credit card, bank transfer, and occasionally check. Payment is due at or before the session unless other arrangements are made.

Ready to find the right option?

If you're unsure which path fits, we can schedule a brief consult to talk through options.

Home About Paths Start

Questions I Frequently Address

Below are practical answers rooted in clinical practice. If you don’t see what you need, email {{EMAIL}} or call {{PHONE}}.

What does an initial session involve?
The first visit is an assessment and collaborative planning conversation: we review your goals, history, and what has brought you in. We usually map priorities and agree on a timeframe for review.
How long do sessions last?
Standard sessions are 50 minutes. Extended intake appointments (75–90 minutes) are available when a deeper review is helpful; these appear as separate options when booking.
Is our work confidential?
Yes. Sessions are confidential with standard legal exceptions (imminent harm, abuse reporting, court orders). Confidentiality limits are discussed and documented during intake.
Do you offer telehealth?
Yes. Telehealth is provided via a secure platform. If in-person is preferred, I have limited office availability in {{CITY}}, {{STATE}}.
What if I’m in crisis?
I am not an emergency provider. If you are an immediate danger to yourself or others, call emergency services or go to the nearest emergency department. If you live in the U.S., you can also call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
Will you share notes with my employer?
I do not share clinical records without your written permission, except when legally required. I will discuss limits to confidentiality during intake.

Therapeutic Foundations

Evidence-informed
Techniques supported by research, adapted to you.
Collaborative
You set goals; I offer structure and tools.
Practical
We track progress and adjust as needed.
{{THERAPIST_NAME}} — {{LICENSE}}

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Evidence vs. Common Myths

Popularity ≠ Evidence

A trendy intervention may help, but we tailor choices to clinical usefulness and your preferences.

Therapy Isn’t Only Talk

We often use behavioral exercises and concrete experiments between sessions to test changes in daily life.

Additional Questions

How do I get records or a letter for my workplace?
I can prepare documentation by request; please allow time and note that this may be a separate billed service. We will discuss scope and content before producing documents.
Do you work with couples or families?
My primary practice is individual adult psychotherapy. I may provide referrals for couples or family work if clinically indicated.
Confidentiality & privacy: Sessions are confidential with legal exceptions. Crisis disclaimer: If you are at immediate risk, call emergency services or go to an emergency department. Begin Care — Book an Appointment

Scheduling options: a short introductory consult or a full intake. If you’re unsure, choose the brief consult and we’ll clarify next steps together.

Available options
  • Introductory Consult — 20 minutes, complimentary for new clients to determine fit.
  • Initial Intake — 75–90 minutes, clinical intake and treatment planning (separate fee).
  • Regular Session — 50-minute ongoing therapy appointments.
Please note: The introductory consult is not a therapy session and is for assessing suitability and answering questions. If you are in crisis call emergency services immediately.
After you request a booking, I will follow up by email with available times and intake paperwork.

What to Expect After Booking

You will receive an email with: confirmation, secure intake forms, a short clinical questionnaire, and a note about fees and cancellation policy. Please complete paperwork before your intake to make our first session most useful.

How I Frame Early Sessions

Early work is assessment-focused: we identify immediate priorities, safety, supports, and practical steps. I use structured, evidence-informed approaches tailored to your situation—no one-size-fits-all prescriptions.

Booking-specific Questions

How quickly can I get an appointment?

Availability varies. Introductory consults are usually scheduled within 1-2 weeks; full intakes may have slightly longer wait times. If you need sooner care, I will suggest alternatives or resources.

What if I need to reschedule?

Please provide at least 48 hours' notice when possible. Late cancellations or missed sessions may incur a fee, which will be discussed during intake.

What technology do you use for telehealth?

I use a secure, HIPAA-compliant video platform. You will receive a link in your appointment confirmation email.

Can I change my session type after booking?

Yes. If you decide you need a full intake instead of a consult (or vice versa), let me know and we will adjust scheduling and fees as needed.

Ready to begin?

Click the booking button to request a time, or email {{EMAIL}} with questions.
